steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Jordi!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Uncle Thiago? What's going on?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Quick, pack up. We have to go.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Wait, what? Where are we going?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: The Inquisition is coming.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: ...What?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: The cultists, the monsters from the sea...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Are we leaving this town for good?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: We?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: No, no, just you. When the Inquisition finds out there are cultists here, the Ægir will be their first target.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: I don't care what happens to the cultists, or even the rest of us... We've lived here too long. We don't know how to live anywhere else.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: But you're different. You've always wanted to see the world outside. You're young and talented.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But, I... this is all so sudden.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: It's an opportunity for change, lad. Your last chance. Be brave.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Even if you somehow survive the Inquisition's interrogation, all that's waiting for you here is a life spent in fear of the ocean and the Sea Terrors.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: If you leave, though, your fate will finally be in your own hands. Not stuck in that little chapel.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: That place is too small for you. You shouldn't just—

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But, I... It's so sudden.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: There's no time to hesitate, lad. You must be strong, like your parents and their parents before them.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Did my parents really give their lives for Iberia?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: We don't have time for this. Come, we must pack.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: It's been so long since we've had a traveling trader stop by... all your clothes are so old. You can buy new ones so easily out there. All the more reason to leave, don't you think?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But why would the Inquisition be looking for Ægir? Couldn't cultists just as well be Liberi or Feline?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Ægir come from the sea, same as the monsters and the disaster.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Wait... have you seen them?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: No, I... I mean, Uncle, you knew? You knew they were here?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Yes... we all knew there was something to the rumors.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Juan was one of them. He went into an empty warehouse to hide from the streets. He was hurt, and... he had no hostility towards me.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Right, because you're Ægir. I know they've gone mad, that they're not normal.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But why? ...Are you sheltering them?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: None of that matters anymore. You'll be leaving soon.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: No, I don't want to.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I... I was born here in Gran Faro. If I run away just to hide from the Inquisition, I... I don't know.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: You what? Do you have any idea what you're saying?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: No Ægir has ever made it back in one piece after the Inquisition gets them! If you're LUCKY, you might return missing a few body parts, or maybe your sanity.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Most simply disappear though. Some say they've been imprisoned, others that they've been executed. No one comes back! No one!

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: The Inquisition will burn everything to the ground in their 'mercy,' before the monsters and cultists even get a chance. Nothing cleanses like fire!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: U-Uncle Thiago, calm down!
The angry old man sees in Jordi the shadow of himself, arriving in this land all those years ago, hoping to construct a new garden out of the ruins.
Decades have passed, and those who were once young are no longer so. Yet what have they built in Gran Faro? What has become of Iberia?
Their efforts have done nothing to change the tidings of fate, and the home that they put so much of their passion into now stands on the precipice of collapse.
A vast helplessness engulfs Thiago, like the dark clouds over the sea.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: No one...

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: No one... no one has ever come back. Not Marin, not anyone else. Gran Faro is already burning. Be it the Inquisition or the monsters, there's no future for us here.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Uncle Thiago...

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: I'll never be able to face your parents if anything happens to you, Jordi.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I... I know, I...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: C-Can I go see the ocean?

steps.name: Tight-Lipped Adherent
steps.text: Gaaaaaaaah!

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Dream now, and may your sleep be full of nightmares.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Leave them to me, Kal'tsit. Soon enough, they will confess where their dark and dank schemes take root.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: No doubt.

steps.name: Alty
steps.text: (Wow, the old man's with you, Doctor?)

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: You are... Alive Until Sunset. A rock band. I must admit I don't understand these new-fangled trends.

steps.name: Alty
steps.text: Have faith in the divinity of song then.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Iberia hasn't recorded a direct sighting of a Feranmut for centuries, much less an interaction. If your music represents your views on human society, then that would certainly pique my interest.

steps.name: Alty
steps.text: We haven't paid attention to that sort of thing since 'Deep Color in the Sea.' It's a topic that's all too familiar, you see.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Ha... I wonder, what music would you put to Iberia? The most surprising thing I've found at my age is how much still surprises me.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: As we discussed, the Inquisition will prepare a means for you to travel to the Eye of Iberia as soon as possible, Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: You will eliminate any obstacles in your path.

steps.name: Alty
steps.text: ...That Sea Terror. The one that's embedded in the guy.

steps.name: Alty
steps.text: There's the scent of an Ægir on it. A different scent though, one more like us. The scent of the sea.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What?
Thiago's steps are small, but quick. He seems burdened by age, yet surprisingly energetic.
It was all Jordi could do to keep up with his pace. He said he wanted to see the ocean.
He did not know why he said that. Even now, he does not know whether it is he who wants to see it, or Thiago.
'I'm an Ægir,' Jordi thinks. 'The sea is my home.'
'But how do I breathe down there? How did my ancestors live underwater?'
Questions pop into his head one after another, questions he had been curious about from a young age. But Thiago is Liberi, and cannot answer his questions.

a.text: The Ægir came from the ocean. Why would they drown in the ocean?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: The sea...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: When was the last time I saw it?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: If the Penal Battalion were still here, they would've taken us in for questioning by now.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: S-Sorry for asking to do this.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: ...It's fine.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Look at the coastline. Barren and decrepit. Decades ago, we had big dreams of building an impregnable fortress here.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Today, there's a Penal Battalion outpost several clicks to the northeast, and another on the cliffs to the west.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Everything else? A lie... or perhaps a dream in the true sense. Reality is before our eyes, reminding us that the old Iberia will never return.
Thiago whistles. Jordi rarely sees him do so.
A change seems to have come over the normally gloomy mayor, turning him into a young worker once again, passionate about building his home.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Tsk, it's all in the past. We failed. Gran Faro is the final resting place of our failures.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: You mentioned your parents, didn't you lad?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I did...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I don't remember much of the ocean. Everyone talks about Ægir and the Islanders, but none of it feels real. I was born on land.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Aye. Your parents, or more accurately your grandparents, came from a place called Ægir, a great country deep beneath the ocean.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: That's where you were from, lad.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Ægir.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Years ago, the dream we had for Gran Faro wasn't the lifeless town you see today. It would have been a fortress, one that laughs at any siege.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: We would have built defenses on the coast around it, protected our country from calamity, heralded her revival, and rebuilt our home. All with our own hands.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: We really thought so.
Jordi does not interrupt. Thiago grows increasingly excited, a light returning to his dull and cloudy eyes.
Every hair on his body stands on end. He changes his posture. The sea breeze brushes against his brow, and he even looks grander somehow.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: The last step of our grand design, spanning half a century, was to return to the Eye of Iberia and relight the lighthouse.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: The lighthouse?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: A relic of the Golden Age, spared from destruction by the Profound Silence.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Not even calamity could break us. We marched ever forward, our hearts filled with hope.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Marin wore that blue hat of hers. She said we'd become heroes, that our names would live on.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Your grandparents, your parents... two generations of Gran Faro gave everything they had for this blueprint. Their greatness should have been immortalized forever.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: But now there's nothing left.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: You see that ship? There used to be many ships at the port. The Penal Battalion should have taken it, but they've forgotten all about it.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: All that's left is some junk, a town out in the middle of nowhere, more troubles than I can count, people stuck in a dead end, and—

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: And that ship.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Yes. That ship.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: My parents, and the grandparents I've never met... were they proud of their duty?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: This isn't the first time you've asked that.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: You asked it when you first learned to talk, and when you started working at the chapel. You asked it many times, pointing at the dust-covered notebooks and schematics at home.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I... I remember.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Yes, lad.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: No matter how many times you ask, my answer is always 'yes.' No matter the outcome, they never lost hope after that great disaster, and gave their all to the cause.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Your parents even volunteered for our final attempt to reach the Eye.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Don't blame them for abandoning you. They were carrying what was left of all our dreams. So many years had come and gone. We HAD to succeed.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: The last we saw of them was when their fleet set sail from right here.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: They were heroes. Marin said we would all become heroes, but now none of us are, except for the dead.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I see...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: So my father and mother...

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: But you know what laid waste to it all? In the midst of despair, we managed to muster the hope to relight the lighthouse. And what came of it?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: The Inquisition. They arrested the Ægir. They said there were Church of the Deep spies among us.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: We were fighting for Iberia, but the Inquisition took everything from us—our pride, our dignity, our dreams... everything.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Do you understand now?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Leave this hopeless town, leave Iberia and go as far as you can. Go to another country, go to a better place.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: There's nothing left here, in Gran Faro.

steps.name: Dan
steps.text: The sea!

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: This is the wrong way. Are we just gonna leave our instruments in that damp room?

steps.name: Dan
steps.text: No, I can smell the waves. The sea is just ahead.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: What do waves smell like?

steps.name: Dan
steps.text: Like cotton.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: Using olfactory vocabulary to express visual elements...

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: But you're right. The sea's right up ahead.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: An Ægir, and of a different breed from the ones who grew up on land. You must be that strange sort of Ægir.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: What did they call you again? Oh right, Abyssal Hunters.
Gladiia frowns. She rarely expresses her emotions in such complex ways.
It came from her instincts as an Abyssal Hunter, as a Consul, as an Ægir technician, as a soldier.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You are... AUS.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You know them.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Yes, by chance.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: Why so mysterious? Well, whatever, I'm just glad our name is known even among the Ægir.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: Alty once visited that ship, following your scent trail. But this is the first time we've met in person.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: I'm Aya, main vocalist of AUS. Dan here is our drummer.

steps.name: Dan
steps.text: Greetings, guests from the sea.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You're of the sea too. A pleasure to meet you.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: When I came to the land, I sought Kal'tsit to learn more about you—about your terrestrial kin.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: Oh... if you're talking about the things on land, then I guess we're kin, technically. Not sure I can say the same about the ones in the sea.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: What are you here for? The doctor?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Just an appointment.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: We seek a way back to Ægir.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: Back to Ægir, huh... The three of you, together?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: We are not so easily separated.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: Aw, what a great friendship. What about the one in the back? Is she shy? Why doesn't she say anything?

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: Something doesn't seem right with her. Her brain is tormented. Is she sick?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You could say so.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: Poor thing.

steps.name: Dan
steps.text: —Mm!

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: What is it, Dan?

steps.name: Dan
steps.text: I just felt something up my spine. Like an electric shock to my brain, then a strange—

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: —Voice.
Unusually quiet, Specter gazes at the sky.
She closes her eyes. Waves brush against chaotic thoughts. This place is far from the coast, but something is touching her consciousness.
It is in the wind, among the clouds, through the land, from the sea.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: A voice. I can hear it.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Hmm... I don't hear anything.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: The music of the sea. The children of the sea are crying.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: It is... a song.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: The scent of Sea Terrors. Lots of them. The town is under attack.

steps.name: Panicking Townsperson
steps.text: H-Hey! How did you get in here?

steps.name: Panicking Townsperson
steps.text: A-Are you an Inquisitor?! The ones you're dragging are—

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Go home.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: These two are under suspicion of colluding with heretics. I am performing my duty as an Iberian Inquisitor.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Leave now, unless you want to be caught up in battle. Their blood will draw enemies.

steps.name: Panicking Townsperson
steps.text: A-An Inquisitor?! When did the Inquisition arrive? W-Were those outsiders your informants?

steps.name: Panicking Townsperson
steps.text: I, I'm not a cultist! I don't have anything to do with those guys!

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Do you know these two?

steps.name: Panicking Townsperson
steps.text: Them? Juan...? It's Juan? I always thought he looked suspicious. He—

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: That's enough.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: No need to torment yourself. Go home, and be sure your doors and windows are locked.

steps.name: Panicking Townsperson
steps.text: A-Alright...

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: You can come out now.

steps.name: Church of the Deep Cultist A
steps.text: An Inquisitor... no, a High Inquisitor!

steps.name: Church of the Deep Cultist B
steps.text: What's the Inquisition doing here?

steps.name: Church of the Deep Cultist A
steps.text: Amaia and Thiago have gone missing. Do the Ægir have something to do with it?

steps.name: Church of the Deep Cultist B
steps.text: You killed Juan, you bastard!

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Not quite, he yet lives. I intend to extract some answers from him.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: You are different from the enemies I know. Your minds are your own, and you are working under clear directions.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: But if you're truly sane and awake, then you should understand—

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: —That you stand no chance against me, nor any other brave soldier of the Inquisition.

steps.name: Church of the Deep Cultist A
steps.text: Tch...

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Why give up your lives? What meaning is there in your futile sacrifice?

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: What have the accursed tides promised you? What are you scheming on this barren shore?

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: I have many questions, enemies of Iberia.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: And I can only hope your god has answers.
